## DNA repair, very simply

Think of DNA as a **book of instructions**:

```text
📖 DNA book
      ↓
💥 A letter is damaged or missing
      ↓
🚨 The cell notices the mistake
      ↓
🛑 The cell pauses
      ↓
🧰 A repair tool fixes it
      ↓
✅ The cell checks the repair
```

Different problems need different tools:

- **Small mistake:** replace one damaged DNA “letter.”
- **Copying mistake:** correct the wrong letter.
- **Large damaged section:** cut it out and replace it.
- **DNA break:** reconnect the broken pieces, sometimes using an undamaged matching copy as a guide.

The **DNA damage response**, or **DDR**, is the cell’s repair-and-safety system. It detects damage and may pause cell division while repair happens. If the damage cannot be handled, the cell may stop dividing or die [DNA damage and repair overview](/education/concepts/cancer-biology/genome-instability-and-repair/dna-damage-and-repair-overview/#how-it-works).

Would you prefer an even simpler cartoon about **one broken DNA strand** or **two broken DNA strands**?
